text:
Diego Morales: Hi team — I accepted the GitHub invite but when I try to push to my assigned repo I get permission denied. My org membership shows as 'Member' but the repo still 404s in the web UI. Anyone ran into this?

Priya (DevEx): Welcome Diego! Which repo are you trying to access, and did you accept the org SSO prompt after signing in with your work account?

Diego Morales: It's `redwood-inference/ml-serving`. I clicked the blue "Authorize SSO" button right after accepting the invite. Web shows me as a member but repo page says "This repository is private" and gives a 404. `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/ml-serving.git` returns `Permission denied (publickey).`

Sam (IT): @Diego can you confirm your SSH key is on the right GitHub account? Sometimes people have two GH accounts and the key is attached to the other one. Check https://github.com/settings/keys

Diego Morales: Ah, I do have an old personal account with the same email on file. My work email was added to both accounts months ago. I didn't realize that would block access.

Priya (DevEx): Yep that collision explains it. Options: 1) Remove the work email from the personal account so the invite maps to your work account; 2) We remove the personal account from the org invite and resend to the work account; 3) We can remove the personal account and transfer team membership. Which do you prefer?

Diego Morales: I'd rather keep my personal account separate. Option 2 please.

Onboarding Bot: New hire checklist updated: GitHub org invite pending (devex action required).

Sam (IT): I'll remove the stray membership and reissue the invite to diego@redwood.ai now. Also make sure 2FA is enabled — org policy requires it. You can enable it at https://github.com/settings/security.

Diego Morales: 2FA is on (auth app).

Sam (IT): Invite resent. Accept it while signed into your work account; using a private/incognito window avoids existing sessions.

Diego Morales: Accepted. I can see the repo now in the web UI and the clone works. `git clone` succeeded. Thanks!

Rachel (Eng): Quick FYI — if you still hit permission denied on push, check that your account is a member of the `ml-infra` team which has push access. You can see teams on the org profile or ping Priya to add you.

Diego Morales: I can see `ml-infra` under my Teams on the org page, and I pushed a tiny branch. `git push origin feature/onboard` worked.

Priya (DevEx): Great. Two small followups: 1) If your personal account still has your work email, consider removing it (github.com/settings/emails) so future invites don't collide. 2) Add your SSH key to your work account if not already there and add a deploy key only where appropriate.

Diego Morales: Removed work email from personal account and added my ssh key to the work account. `ssh -T git@github.com` returns "Hi diego! You've successfully authenticated". All good now.

Onboarding Bot: Onboarding checklist updated: GitHub access confirmed.

Priya (DevEx): Welcome to Redwood, Diego :tada: If you want a quick repo map and starter issues, DM me and I'll drop the onboarding PR checklist and required READMEs.

Diego Morales: Thanks everyone, appreciate the fast help!
